question.text: Will a second televised debate between Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen be scheduled by November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, by 23:59 Taipei time (UTC+8) on November 13, 2026, a specific calendar date has been publicly announced for a second televised debate between Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) and Puma Shen (沈伯洋), as reported on [CNA's 2026 election topic page](https://www.cna.com.tw/topic/newstopic/5100.aspx) or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). "Second televised debate" means any debate other than the October 31, 2026 TVBS/SET event: an event produced by a media outlet and broadcast on a television channel or that outlet's live online stream, in which both candidates appear together in a debate format — taking questions from each other and/or from journalists, as in the October 31 event — rather than separate solo appearances such as a 政見發表會 (policy presentation). A date counts as announced only if it is reported as agreed by both campaigns, or as confirmed by the hosting outlet(s)/organizer with both candidates participating; a date proposed or accepted by only one campaign does not count, and an announced date still counts even if the debate is later postponed or cancelled. If no such date has been announced by the deadline, this question resolves NO.
question.fine_print: Any host qualifies — a single broadcaster, a consortium of media outlets, or another organizer — provided both campaigns are confirmed participants. If several additional debates are announced by the deadline, the announcement of any one of them suffices.

research:
Short version: as of November 4, 2026, there is still no date for a second Chiang-Shen debate. Chiang says he is open to one, but his campaign has now set conditions before it will even negotiate.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03/04: CNA's election topic page has four headlines on the Taipei debate, dated Nov 2-3. None gives a date for a second debate. The newest, from Nov 3, 13:02, reads "蔣萬安：傾向參加第2次辯論會 談定形式、時間就願意": Chiang leans toward attending once format and timing are agreed. Other headlines: "第2場辯論？蔣萬安：由團隊協調" (Nov 2, his team will coordinate) and "第2場辯論？沈伯洋：辯論提問蔣萬安都不答" (Nov 2, Shen says Chiang does not answer questions). The page also lists a Kaohsiung forum on Nov 14 billed as having no questions and no debate, so it is not the same kind of event. [CNA topic](https://www.cna.com.tw/topic/newstopic/5100.aspx)
- There is no data file behind this page. Resolution depends on news reports.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. No date has been agreed by both campaigns or confirmed by a host. Both sides say they are willing in principle, but on Nov 4 Chiang's side added preconditions.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Chiang's campaign manager, KMT legislator Lo Chih-chiang (羅智強), said he "will not negotiate a debate with a camp lacking integrity" (不和沒有誠信的陣營協商辯論). His conditions:
  - Shen's campaign chief Wu Szu-yao (吳思瑤) must publicly apologize to TVBS and SET for what Lo calls three lies during the first-debate talks: the time slot, the cross-examination claim, and the advance questions.
  - The debate consent form must include an "integrity clause".
  
  He also challenged Wu to agree to release TVBS's recording of the negotiations. He confirmed receiving a second-debate invitation from the Liberty Times and others, and noted that with under a month left, preparation is hard. Wu and Lo have exchanged LINE contacts. [NOWnews](https://www.nownews.com/news/6889207), [TVBS](https://news.tvbs.com.tw/politics/4045571), [ETtoday](https://www.ettoday.net/news/20261104/3265981.htm), [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/124652/9855907), [China Times](https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20261104001247-260407)
- 2026-11-04: Taisounds reported that unnamed print media had invited both candidates to a second debate. No dates were proposed, and the article carries no reply from Shen's camp. [Taisounds](https://www.taisounds.com/news/content/70/297768)
- 2026-11-04: I found no formal reply from Wu or Shen's campaign to the apology demand. Separately, Shen has said his side accepts whatever time and format the host proposes. [Storm](https://www.storm.mg/article/11178338)
- 2026-11-03: On Shen Chun-hua's TV program, Chiang said he "leans toward attending" a second debate and is confident about debating. If one happens, he said the two teams should first settle time and details, as they did for the first. [UDN](https://udn.com/vote2026/story/124652/9853637), [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1932643)
- 2026-11-02: Shen asked for a second debate that includes immediate answers to media questions. Chiang said he understood why Shen wanted one, but criticized him for wasting the first. [Newtalk](https://newtalk.tw/news/view/2026-11-02/1068755)
- 2026-10-31: After the first debate, 10 outlets issued a joint statement inviting both candidates to a second one: Liberty Times, CTV, TTV, FTV, Mirror TV, CTS, ETtoday, EBC, Era/ERA One "and others". They proposed no date and set no deadline, only asking the camps to respond "as soon as possible" and send negotiators. [China Times](https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20261031003050-260407)
- Since the first debate there has been a dispute over questions being shared in advance. Shen admitted he had seen the media's questions beforehand. [Yahoo](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B-%E6%88%91%E6%98%A8%E6%97%A5%E8%BE%AF%E8%AB%96%E5%AE%8C%E5%BF%83%E6%83%85%E9%9D%9E%E5%B8%B8%E6%B2%AE%E5%96%AA-%E6%88%91%E4%BA%8B%E5%89%8D%E6%9C%89%E7%9C%8B%E9%81%8E%E5%AA%92%E9%AB%94%E6%8F%90%E5%95%8F%E9%A1%8C%E7%9B%AE-032157574.html)
- Post-debate polls conflict:
  - 2026-11-02, ETtoday: Chiang leads by 11.3 points. [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/124652/9851526)
  - 2026-11-02, Taiwan Strategy Research Institute (seen as pro-DPP): Shen leads by 17.3 points. [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1932117)

## 4. Base rates
- For the first debate, outlets announced a joint debate on Oct 11 and the date was fixed on Oct 15, after two rounds of talks: about 4 days from formal talks to a date, but weeks of public fighting before that.
- Custom in Taipei races has been one televised debate plus the government-run policy presentations, which is what Chiang cited at first. I found no systematic data on how often a second Taipei mayoral debate gets held.
- The 2022 Taipei race had one televised debate. That is from memory and I did not verify it here.
- Candidates who are ahead usually have less reason to agree to more debates. Markets currently price Chiang as the favourite.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on a second debate.
- Related markets, fetched 2026-11-04:
  - Kalshi, Taipei winner: Chiang 0.64, Shen 0.36.
  - Polymarket, Taipei winner: Chiang 0.665, Shen 0.32.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (by Nov 13, 23:59 Taipei time)
- Watch for any reply from Wu or Shen's camp to the apology and integrity-clause demands, and for any coordination meeting called by the 10 outlets or the Liberty Times group.
- 2026-11-12: The Central Election Commission publishes the official candidate list.
- 2026-11-13: The official campaign period and the government-run policy presentations begin. New Taipei's presentation is on Nov 13. [FTV](https://ftvnews.com.tw/news/detail/2026B02W0543)
- 2026-11-18: The polling blackout begins. A debate would realistically have to fall around Nov 14-27, so any date would need to be fixed soon, which puts the deadline near the decision point.

- Time pressure: the official campaign period starts November 13 and polling ends November 27, so if a two-week prep lead time applies, a debate would need to be fixed soon. This is my inference from the stated lead time.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) There are about 9 to 10 days left, until 23:59 Taipei time on November 13, 2026. For Yes, a specific date for a second Chiang-Shen televised debate must be publicly announced, either as agreed by both campaigns or as confirmed by the host with both candidates participating.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of November 4 there is no date and no coordination meeting has been held. Chiang's campaign manager has also attached preconditions to even starting negotiations.

(c) Base rate: Taipei mayoral races recently have had only one televised debate (2022, and by custom one debate plus the government-run policy presentations). The 2014 race had several debates, but that was unusual. Across similar races, a leading incumbent agreeing to a second debate, with a date fixed inside a roughly 10-day window, happens about 20-30% of the time.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On November 3, Chiang said he "leans toward attending" a second debate once format and time are agreed.
  - On October 13 he said a second debate was possible.
  - Ten outlets issued a joint invitation on October 31, and the Liberty Times group sent another invitation.
  - Shen accepts any time and format the host proposes.
  - The two campaign chiefs have exchanged LINE contacts.
  - The first debate went from formal talks to a fixed date in about 4 days, so a quick deal is possible.
- **For No:**
  - On November 4, Lo Chih-chiang refused to negotiate unless Wu Szu-yao publicly apologizes to TVBS and SET for "three lies" and the consent form includes an "integrity clause". The DPP campaign is very unlikely to accept that apology.
  - Lo also noted that with under a month left, preparation is hard.
  - Chiang leads in the markets (about 64-66%), so he has little incentive to debate again.
  - The first debate itself took weeks of public fighting before a date was set.
  - Even if a debate is eventually agreed, the date could be fixed after November 13 for a debate in the November 14-27 window.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Wu refuses to apologize, and both camps trade blame over "integrity" and leaked questions. Chiang keeps saying he is "willing in principle", but the official campaign period starts on November 13 with no date fixed, and the debate never happens or is agreed only later.
- **Yes:** Media pressure and Chiang's "leaning toward attending" lead to a coordination meeting around November 6-10. Lo's demands are quietly softened, for example into a mutual integrity clause, and the outlets announce a date such as November 21 or 22, before the deadline.

(f) I start from about 25%. Chiang's stated willingness and the strong pressure from the media consortium pull upward. The explicit apology precondition, which looks like a stalling tactic by the leading camp, and the short window pull down more strongly. Announcements that land after November 13 would also not count. Overall I move slightly down from the base rate.

Probability: 20%

(a) About 9-10 days remain, until 23:59 Taipei time on November 13, 2026. For Yes, both campaigns must agree on a specific calendar date for a second joint televised debate, or a host must confirm a date with both candidates participating. That has to happen after negotiations that have not yet started.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. No date exists, no coordination meeting has been held, and Chiang's camp has now attached preconditions to even negotiating.

(c) Base rate: Taipei mayoral races usually have one televised debate plus the government-run policy presentations. As far as I recall, the 2022 race had just one debate. Front-running incumbents rarely agree to extra debates late in a campaign. When a second debate is "open in principle" but unscheduled three to four weeks before the vote, it gets scheduled perhaps 25-30% of the time.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Oct 13 and Nov 3: Chiang said a second debate is possible and that he "leans toward attending" once format and timing are agreed.
  - Oct 31: ten media outlets issued a joint invitation, and the Liberty Times invitation has been received.
  - Shen will accept any format, and the campaign managers have exchanged LINE contacts.
  - For the first debate, it took only about 4 days from formal talks to a fixed date.
- For No:
  - Nov 4: Lo Chih-chiang said he "will not negotiate with a camp lacking integrity." He demands that Wu Szu-yao publicly apologize to TVBS and SET, and that the consent form include an "integrity clause." The DPP side is unlikely to accept a public apology.
  - Lo also noted that preparation is hard with under a month left.
  - Chiang leads in most polls and markets (about 64-66%), so he gains little from another debate.
  - The campaign period starts Nov 13 and the polling blackout Nov 18, which leaves little room.

(e) No scenario: Wu refuses to apologize, both sides trade blame over integrity, the media consortium never convenes talks, and the deadline passes with Chiang saying the schedule is full.

Yes scenario: Shen's camp, wanting the debate badly, issues a carefully worded statement or accepts the integrity clause. The media group convenes talks around Nov 8-10 and fixes a date around Nov 20-25 before Nov 13.

(f) I start at about 25%. Chiang's softer public wording argues for slightly higher. But the Nov 4 preconditions look like a classic run-out-the-clock tactic from the front-runner's camp, and the window is short, so I adjust down to about 18%. There is no direct market to anchor on.

Probability: 18%

(a) Time and what is needed for Yes: The deadline is November 13, 2026, 23:59 Taipei time, about 9 to 10 days away. For Yes, a specific date for a second Chiang-Shen debate must be publicly announced in that window. The date must be agreed by both campaigns, or confirmed by the hosting outlet(s) with both candidates participating. The event must be a media-produced, two-candidate debate format other than the October 31 TVBS/SET event.

(b) Status quo: No date exists. On November 4, Chiang's campaign manager Lo Chih-chiang set preconditions:
- an apology from Shen's campaign chief Wu Szu-yao
- an "integrity clause" in the consent form

The status quo outcome is No.

(c) Base rate: Taipei custom is one televised debate plus the CEC presentations. That held in 2022, from memory. Frontrunners rarely agree to extra debates late in a campaign, especially when their team is publicly stalling. Second debates in Taiwanese metropolitan mayoral races where the leader resisted happen perhaps 15-25% of the time. I use a base rate of about 20%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Chiang said "yes" to a second debate on October 13, said he "leans toward attending" on November 3, and said his team will coordinate on November 2.
  - Ten outlets issued a joint invitation on October 31, the Liberty Times group sent its own invitation, and the outlets keep up the pressure.

  - Lo noted that with under a month left, preparation is hard, which reads as a classic stalling signal.
  - Chiang is the market favourite at about 0.64-0.67 and has little incentive to debate again.
  - The calendar is compressed: the campaign period opens on November 13 and the polling blackout starts on November 18.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: The two sides trade accusations over the apology demand, no coordination meeting yields a date, and by mid-November Chiang's camp says the schedule is full and points to the CEC presentations.
- Yes: Under media and public pressure, Chiang's team drops or softens its preconditions. A coordination meeting with the 10-outlet consortium fixes a date around November 20-25, announced before November 13.

(f) Adjustment: I start at 20%. Chiang's repeated public statements of willingness, and the existence of a ready host consortium, push upward somewhat. The November 4 preconditions are a strong delaying signal, and the leader's incentives push back down. With the short window and stall tactics, I land near 20%.

Probability: 20%

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of November 4 there is no date, no coordination meeting and no agreed host. The Chiang camp has also added new preconditions.

(c) Base rate: recent Taipei mayoral races (2018, 2022) each had one main televised debate. Chiang himself cites one debate as the custom. Incumbents who lead in the polls usually limit debates. For "leading incumbent agrees to a second debate," I put the base rate at about 15-25%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
